mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicates elevated inflation, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy, thereby reducing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL is above 200, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and SPX 60d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and SPX 5d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts and retail sales signals a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) and SPX 60d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite, leading to negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and SPX 5d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC between PAYEMS and SPX 20d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110 indicates a contraction in manufacturing and services sectors, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 110, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and SPX 5d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts and GDP growth signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and GDPC1 decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST * GDPC1) and SPX 60d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (as indicated by a sharp decline in industrial production), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate output, leading to negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines by >1.0% in 1 month, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and SPX 5d returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
